source: XET Little Fox licensed subtitle import
title: Wild Adventures

subtitle.text: It's early morning in the African desert.
Most of the meerkats are still asleep in their burrow.
But Max is awake.
"I'm hungry!"
His big sister, Zara, opens one eye.
"Shh!" she whispers. "Go back to sleep!"
Max's little brother, Stripe, yawns.
"Is it time to get up?"
Max grins. "I'm going hunting!"
"Meerkats don't hunt alone," Zara says.
"Besides, Mom still has to catch scorpions for you."
"I can catch a scorpion by myself," Max says.
Zara rolls over. "Whatever."
"I'll show her!" Max thinks.
He sneaks to the burrow entrance.
Max steps outside and sniffs the ground.
"No bugs here . . ." Max thinks.
He wanders farther into the warm desert.
He sniffs again.
"This is fun," he thinks. "I'm hunting by myself."
Finally he smells something.
He digs up a tiny worm. "Yum!"
But Max is still hungry.
Suddenly—
screech! Max looks up. "A goshawk!"
He sees a bolt-hole and takes off.
The bird dives after him!
But Max leaps inside just in time!
Max gulps. "That was close.
Maybe Zara was right."
When the hawk is gone, Max decides to go home.
Outside the bolt-hole, Max freezes.
Hisss! A cobra rises in front of him!
It swings its head, ready to strike.
Max jumps out of the way.
"Chee-chee-chee!" he calls.
Stomp! Stomp! Stomp!
The meerkat mob rushes over.
Their fur puffs up as they surround the snake.
They growl and hiss.
The snake slithers off fast.
Mom frowns at Max. "You can't go out by yourself."
"I told you meerkats don't hunt alone," Zara says.
"But I was really hungry," Max says.
Mom sighs. "The mob has to stick together.
That's how we survive."
"Okay," Max says. "Since we're all here . . .
Can we go hunting now?"
It's morning in the desert.
The meerkats come out of their burrow.
Some clean the entrance.
Others warm up in the sun.
Max and Stripe run around.
"I'll eat the most food today," Max says.
Stripe jumps. "I'll eat more!"
Zara sighs. "There isn't a contest."
Suddenly the sky turns dark. Plop. Plop.
"Ugh! Rain again!" Max says.
"It's rainy season," Zara says.
"Everyone, go inside," Mom says.
The mob returns to the sleeping room.
"I hope the rain stops soon," Max says.
Zara curls up. "I'm taking a nap."
"Let's have a digging contest," Max says.
He looks at Stripe. "Fastest paws win!"
"Not in here," Mom says.
Max and Stripe find a side tunnel.
They start to dig in one wall.
Sand sprays everywhere.
Then the wall falls.
"Look!" Stripe says. "A secret tunnel!"
Max grins. "Let's see where it goes."
Stripe frowns. "What about the digging contest?" "Exploring
is more fun," Max says. "Come on!" They
go into the tunnel. It
leads to more tunnels. "I
didn't know our burrow was so big," Stripe says. They
squeeze into a tiny tunnel. Crunch!
The tunnel crumbles behind them! "Uh-oh,"
Stripe says. "How do we go back?" Max
looks around. "I don't know." Stripe
moans. "We'll be lost forever." Then—
scratch, scratch!
"It's a dung beetle!" Max says.
"They clean our burrow's toilet room.
Maybe it can lead us there!"
After a while Stripe sniffs the air.
"I smell meerkat poo," he says.
Max grins. "We're close to the toilet room."
Soon they find the mob.
Everyone is at the burrow entrance.
"The rain stopped," Mom says.
Outside, near a puddle, Max sees worms.
"The rain brought snacks," he says.
Stripe runs. "I'll eat the most worms."
"No, you won't!" Max says. "I'll eat them all first!"
The meerkat mob is out hunting.
"Can I be a lookout today?" Max asks.
Zara shakes her head. "Lookouts have an important job.
They watch for enemies while others hunt."
Max puffs out his chest. "I'm ready!"
"Zara will be the first lookout," Mom says.
"Watch what she does."
Zara climbs to the top of a tall rock.
"No hawks, no jackals!" Zara calls. "All clear!"
Later it's time to change lookouts.
"Please, Mom?" Max begs.
Mom sighs. "Okay. But you must pay attention."
"Yes!" Max runs off and climbs a rock.
He stands tall, looking around.
"The Great Max is on duty!"
He watches the sky and the ground.
"No enemies in the sky," Max thinks.
"And nothing is happening on the ground."
Finally Max sighs. "This is boring."
Suddenly a lizard crawls by.
Max licks his lips. "There's a tasty treat."
He frowns. "But I have to watch for enemies . . ."
Then he grins. "Maybe I can catch it quickly."
He jumps toward it, but the lizard takes off.
The lizard zigs and zags as Max chases it.
Then it shoots into the grass.
"It got away!" Max groans.
He looks around. "Where is everyone?"
Soon Max finds the rest of the mob.
They are coming out of a bolt-hole.
"Where did you go?" Zara asks.
"I . . . er . . .," Max says.
"Well, a big hawk was hunting us!" Stripe says.
"What?" Max gulps.
"Yeah," Zara says. "Our lookout disappeared.
So I had to make the warning call!"
"That's enough, Zara," Mom says.
"As for you, Max, Lookouts can't—"
"Leave their post," Max says.
"I know. I'm sorry."
Mom pats him. "Out here, we must protect each other."
"Next time I'll stay put," Max says.
"And I'll be the best lookout ever!"
The mob is heading back to the burrow.
Max groans. "I found only a few ants."
Suddenly Mom stops. "Jackal prints."
"They lead home," Stripe says.
"Zara's at home," Max says.
"She's babysitting the pups."
The mob races to the burrow.
Max sees Zara outside with two meerkat pups.
"Jackals sniffed around our burrow," Zara says.
"We hid until they left."
"Jackals are dangerous neighbors," Max says.
Mom nods. "And our food is running low here."
"That means it's time to move," Zara says.
"Move?" Max cries. "But I love it here.
My favorite nap rock is here!"
"A safe mob keeps moving," Zara says.
"We have other burrows," Mom says.
"You'll like the new one, Max."
The mob walks across the hot desert.
Mom and Zara help the pups.
Later the sky turns red.
Everyone is tired and hungry.
Max sees something in the distance.
"Whoa. That rock looks perfect for naps."
"Our new burrow is right behind it," Mom says.
Max smiles. "Great!"
Stripe chomps a beetle. "There's plenty of food."
"I'll check if the burrow is safe," Zara says.
The others keep moving.
Soon they hear Zara. "All clear!"
Then a shadow flies over them.
Max looks up. "Eagle!"
The mob shoots toward the new burrow.
Max starts to run.
But Mom is far behind with the pups!
Above, the eagle is circling.
Max runs back toward Mom.
He grabs one of the pups.
"Now run!" Mom shouts. "Fast!"
As they take off, the eagle swoops lower.
Whew! They make it to the burrow!
"Great job, Max," Mom says. "You saved the day."
Later Max goes outside. "The eagle's gone."
"Do you like the new burrow?" Mom asks.
Max grins. "I'll tell you after I have a snack.
And a nap on my new nap rock."
It is morning in a forest in India.
Loud trumpeting wakes up Kabir, a young elephant.
Kabir stands up and trumpets too.
"Mother, why is everyone so happy?"
Mother smiles. "A baby was born last night.
Would you like to see her?"
"Okay," Kabir says.
Baby Isha stands under her mother.
The herd gathers around them.
Grandmother and the aunts touch Isha with their trunks.
She takes some steps and stumbles.
Kabir and his cousin Rishi try to get close to Isha.
The aunts gently push them away.
Kabir frowns. "What's so special about babies?"
"Yeah!" Rishi says. "She can barely walk."
Kabir and Rishi play, butting heads.
"Let's go look for leaves," Kabir says.
Rishi grins. "We're not babies!
We can find our own food."
The two young elephants walk through the forest.
They play and throw sticks at each other.
Kabir stuffs a leafy branch in his mouth.
"Yum! I could eat this whole tree!"
"Save some for . . ." Suddenly Rishi freezes.
"What's wrong?" Kabir whispers.
"I hear twigs snapping," Rishi whispers.
Kabir lifts his trunk. "I smell . . . danger!"
Fear shoots through Kabir.
A tiger is crouching in the brush!
He sends out a cry. "We need help!"
Rishi cries out too.
Kabir hears pounding steps.
An elephant crashes through the forest—Aunt Mehda!
She charges at the tiger.
It races away and disappears.
"That was scary!" Kabir says.
"You got here fast!" Rishi says.
"I followed you," Aunt Medha says.
She smacks Rishi and Kabir lightly with her trunk.
"Remember to stay with the herd."
The three walk back together.
"We'll leave the herd when we're older," Rishi says.
"True," Aunt Mehda says.
Kabir grins. "But now we're still young . . .
So, thanks for following us!"
The elephants are feeding on the grassland.
There is lots of fresh grass here.
"Yum!" Kabir thinks.
He pulls up another clump and shakes off the dirt.
Then he stuffs it into his mouth.
As Kabir eats, he watches Aunt Dhwani.
Her trunk is short.
She injured it when she was young.
The others must feed her.
"Dhwani would go hungry without us," Mother says.
Kabir nods and pulls a branch from a tree.
"Here, Auntie." He feeds her the branch.
"Thank you, little one," Dhwani says.
Suddenly the adults freeze.
Their trunks go up to sniff the air.
Kabir lifts his trunk too.
He smells something. "Hmm. What is it?"
Suddenly the adults make a circle around the young elephants.
The sound of animals running fills the air.
"What's happening?" Isha says. "I'm scared!"
She sucks on her trunk.
Kabir wraps his trunk around Isha.
"The adults are making an alert circle to protect us."
A large group of wild pigs appears.
In the outside circle, the adults face the pigs.
In the middle, the little ones are safe.
Then Kabir hears a loud trumpeting sound.
It is Grandmother.
"She's warning them to get away," Kabir whispers.
"Are pigs really dangerous?" Isha asks.
"Not really," Kabir says. "But it's a big group.
And they like to eat our food."
Grandmother raises her head and spreads her ears.
Now she looks huge!
Then . . . Grandmother charges the pigs.
Dhwani charges, too, and the pigs run off.
Soon everyone returns to eating.
Kabir walks up to Dhwani. "That was great!
You protected us—and our food."
Dhwani nuzzles him with her trunk.
"Soon I'll be able to charge enemies too!" Kabir thinks.
Kabir wakes up hungry. "Breakfast time!"
He starts to eat some grass.
Other elephants are eating too.
But something is wrong.
Kabir frowns. "There used to be lots of fresh grass.
Now the grassland is almost bare!"
Mother nods. "We've been here for several days.
It's getting hard to find food."
Kabir goes into the forest to look for bamboo.
Rishi is eating some stalks.
"You ate it all!" Kabir says.
Rishi shakes his head. "Not much was left."
Kabir returns to Mother.
She sticks her trunk in his mouth. "Come with me.
We're going to find more food."
All the elephants spread out, looking.
Kabir and Mother walk through the forest.
Kabir looks back.
"Where's the herd?" he thinks.
"We're almost to a good spot," Mother says.
They come to a grove of trees.
The ground is covered with dates!
Kabir picks up one with his trunk. "Yum!"
They spend the day eating dates.
Suddenly Kabir looks around nervously.
"Where's our herd?"
Mother rumbles a call to the others.
"They'll call back to us," Kabir thinks.
Kabir pushes his ears forward to listen.
But he doesn't hear anything.
"Maybe they're too far away to hear us," Mother says.
She tries another call.
At first, Kabir and Mother don't hear anything.
Then Kabir remembers what to do.
"We should listen with our feet!
We can hear faraway sounds better that way!"
Mother nods and presses her feet to the ground.
They both stand very still.
Suddenly Kabir feels a rumbling in his feet.
Grandmother is far away, but Kabir hears her!
They follow the sound.
At last Kabir spots the herd.
"Grandmother!" Kabir raises his trunk.
"Our feet heard your call!"
Kabir and Rishi are walking with the herd.
Isha is falling behind.
"Wait up!" Isha calls, running to them.
"I'm so tired," Isha says.
Kabir nods. "It's very hot.
But we need to keep moving to find food."
The herd walks and walks.
Insects buzz and bite them.
Rishi scoops up dirt to fling on his back.
"This keeps the bugs away," he says.
Isha copies him. "Stay away, bugs!"
Kabir sniffs the air. "Water!
We can finally drink and cool off!"
The herd comes to a wide river.
All the elephants go in. Splash!
To drink, they suck up water with their trunks.
Then they spray it in their mouths.
"Ahh!" Kabir says happily.
Kabir sinks underwater.
He keeps his trunk above the water to breathe.
The young elephants start to play.
They squirt and chase each other.
Then Grandmother and the aunties cross the river.
They climb out and walk away.
The others start to follow.
"I'll catch up later," Kabir calls.
Mother spins around, frowning. "Come with me, Kabir."
"I'll be fine!" Kabir says.
"One day I'll leave the herd anyway, remember?"
Mother walks off slowly.
Kabir floats down the river for a while.
Then he swims to the bank.
He tries to climb out, but it is too steep!
He slips back into the water.
Kabir tries again—he can't get out!
"Help!" Kabir calls.
Mother sees him.
She races to the riverbank.
So do some aunties.
Two big elephants stand behind Kabir.
They push him up the riverbank.
Kabir climbs out. "Phew! Thanks!"
Isha hurries over. "Are you really leaving one day?"
"Yes," Kabir says. "Males leave the herd around age 12.
But for now . . . " He smiles.
"I'm staying with you!"
It's a cold winter in Antarctica.
Emperor penguin dads huddle together, keeping their chicks warm.
The moms left weeks ago to find food.
Suddenly a chick peeks out of her dad's pouch.
"I'm hungry again," Pia says.
Dad feeds Pia some milk from his throat.
"Mom will be back soon with food," Dad says.
Pia tries to wiggle out. "I want to explore!"
"Pia! Stay on my feet," Dad says.
"It's very cold—and you don't have long feathers yet."
Pia sighs. "I wish they would grow faster."
"Be patient, little one," Dad says.
Soon Dad takes a nap.
"I'll just look outside a little," Pia thinks.
She leans out farther this time.
Whoosh! A big gust of wind hits her face.
"Whoa!" Pia slips off Dad's feet!
She tumbles down a snowy hill.
The cold ice stings her belly!
"Help!" Pia cries.
Dad rushes to find her.
He puts her back on his feet.
"You must stay here."
Pia warms up soon, but Dad still seems worried.
"We got separated from the huddle.
Now we have to get back."
Dad begins to climb the hill.
Whoosh! The icy wind blows.
"I see the huddle!" Dad says.
As they join the huddle, Pia hears something.
"That's your mom's call!" Dad says.
Dad calls back.
Pia carefully looks out.
A penguin is coming toward them.
Pia is meeting Mom for the first time!
Dad smiles. "Our Pia loves to explore."
Mom laughs. "I was the same way as a chick."
Mom puts Pia on her feet.
She feeds Pia fish she stored in her stomach.
"Yum," Pia says.
"My turn to find fish," Dad says.
"Bye, Dad!" Pia waves to him.
"I promise—I'll stay right here!"
Pia sits on her mother's feet.
"When can I learn to walk, Mom?"
But Mom isn't listening—she's watching a large seabird.
"Stay still, Pia."
"Why?" Pia asks.
"That's a skua," Mom says. "Beware—they eat young chicks."
The bird swoops over the colony and flies away.
"Why did it leave?" Pia asks.
"Predators watch for movement," Mom says.
"Oh," Pia says. "Um, can I try walking now?"
"Sure," Mom says.
Pia hops off Mom's feet and takes a step.
Pia wobbles but stays on her feet.
A smaller chick watches her. "I'm Em.
Wow! You're so good at walking!"
"I can teach you," Pia says.
Em takes one step . . . and falls over.
"Try again," Pia says. "Like this."
Soon Pia and Em are walking together.
"Let's race!" Pia says.
The two chicks waddle fast.
Em falls down and giggles. "You win."
"Look out!" A large chick is sliding toward them!
He crashes into Pia and Em and grins.
"Whoa! That was amazing!"
Pia scowls. "You almost hurt us!
Are you okay, Em?"
"Sorry!" the big chick says. "I'm Flip.
I like sliding fast but didn't mean to hurt anyone."
"I'm okay," Em says.
"Why are you sliding?" Pia asks.
Flip grins. "It's fun.
Sliding is much faster than walking."
"Let's try it," Pia says.
The three chicks lie on their bellies.
They push off with their feet. "Whee!"
Suddenly Pia hears an alarm call. "Skua!"
Em gulps. "Skuas eat chicks!"
Flip squawks. "What if it grabs us?"
Pia's heart pounds.
She thinks of what Mom said.
"Drop down and stay still," Pia says.
The three chicks lie very, very still.
The skua swoops low—and then leaves!
"You saved us, Pia," Flip says.
Em nods. "Thanks."
"You're welcome." Pia grins. "Now let's slide some more!"
One day Pia's mom has big news.
"Dad and I are going to the sea for food.
We'll be back next week."
"Oh," Pia says. "What will I do?"
"You'll stay here with the other chicks," Dad says.
He points to a stern-looking penguin.
"Dorsa is in charge while we're gone."
Em's parents are leaving too.
"Wait!" Em cries as she waddles after them.
"I want to come with you!"
"It's okay, Em," Pia says. "I'm here."
"Me too," Flip says. "Want to go sliding?"
Em watches her parents leave and sighs. "Okay."
The three friends slide for a while.
Then it gets dark, and an icy wind blows.
"Brr." Flip shivers. "It's really cold!"
"I miss my parents," Em whispers.
"Let's find Dorsa," Pia says.
They look for Dorsa and the other chicks.
Whoosh! The wind blows so hard, they can't see well.
"We need to find a huddle—fast!" Flip calls.
"I know," Pia says.
She glances back at Em.
The tiny penguin can't keep up.
Pia gulps. "This is bad—Em could freeze!"
"Finally!" Pia shouts.
She spots Dorsa and the other chicks.
They are all huddling together.
Pia and her friends join them, but Em keeps shivering.
Pia knows they must do something.
"It's much warmer in the middle—let's go!"
Pia spots an opening and charges forward.
Another chick blocks her. "Hey!"
Pia stands tall. "We want a turn in the middle!"
Suddenly she hears Dorsa. "Make room—now!
We huddle to keep everyone warm."
The chick moves away.
In the middle Em smiles. "I feel better now."
"Good!" Flip pants. "Because I'm really hot!"
Pia laughs. "Time to give others a turn here."
One day Pia leaves the colony.
The young penguins are walking toward the sea.
"This is so exciting!" Pia says.
"We have waterproof feathers now."
Flip grins. "That means we can swim!"
"I don't want to swim," Em says softly.
"That's how we'll find food," Pia says.
"And escape enemies."
Flip smiles. "I'm going to dive right in."
Pia gets more excited as they march on.
Then up ahead, she sees it. "The sea!"
She races to the edge of the ice.
"Look out!" someone cries. "Leopard seals!"
A seal leaps out of the water.
Pia gasps and moves back, barely escaping its jaws!
"Let's keep going!" a chick says. "It's not safe here."
The penguins start marching again.
Crack! Ahead of them, some ice breaks.
"Yikes!" Flip almost falls into the water.
He laughs. "Maybe I'll just dive in here."
"No!" somebody cries. "You could get stuck under the ice!" "The
sea is dangerous," Em says. Pia
nods. "You're right. We
have to be careful." The
group marches on, but soon everyone gets hungry. Flip
stops and grins. "This looks like a safe spot. Here
I go!" He dives in. Pia
dives in too. In
the sea she knows exactly what to do. She
tucks her feet back, pushing herself with her flippers. She
dives down for some krill. Soon
everyone but Em is zooming through the water. "Em,
come in!" Pia calls. "Um,
soon," Em says. "The
krill is really good," Pia says. Suddenly—
splash! Em dives in!
"I'm swimming!" Em cries.
Pia grins. "You did it!"
And so did Pia.
She can swim and find food by herself now.
She can escape enemies.
Best of all she can explore—all on her own.
It is a warm day on a sandy beach.
Beneath the sand, a baby green sea turtle is hatching.
"Let me out!" Jade cries.
She has a special egg tooth.
She uses it to peck at the eggshell. Crack!
Jade is free!
About a hundred other hatchlings are in the nest too.
"I'm Olive," one says. "We're sisters."
"What do we do now?" Jade asks.
Olive shrugs. "Everyone is waiting here for now."
Later the warm sand cools.
One hatchling starts to dig up through the sand.
"Let's dig up too!" Jade says.
The hatchlings dig for hours.
At last Jade breaks through!
The air feels cool and fresh.
Jade can't see very well, so everything is a blur.
But there is light in one direction.
"Let's go that way."
Jade uses her tiny flippers to move across the sand.
The other hatchlings move too.
"Where are we going?" Olive asks.
"I don't know," Jade says.
"But I'll know the place when I see it."
Soon driftwood blocks their way.
"We have to go around it," Jade says.
"I'm so tired!" Olive moans.
"We can do it," Jade says.
A large crab comes toward them.
It snaps its claws!
Jade gulps and pushes Olive away.
"Phew!" Olive says.
Next, gulls dive toward the hatchlings. Squawk!
"Hurry!" Olive shoves Jade aside.
At last the two hatchlings reach the ocean.
Jade dives into a breaking wave.
She gets carried into deeper water.
"Olive? Where are you?" she cries.
Jade can see much better underwater.
But hatchlings are everywhere!
Which one is Olive?
"Here I am, Jade!" Olive swims over.
"What now?" Olive asks.
Jade shoots through the water with her strong flippers.
It feels great!
"Now we swim, swim, swim!"
Jade and Olive are swimming through the shallows.
They are with some other hatchlings.
"Look out!" one yells.
Big fish—dangerous snappers—dart toward the hatchlings!
"Go, Olive!" Jade says.
The sisters use their front flippers to swim.
Their shells are shaped like a heart.
This shape helps them zoom through the sea.
Soon the hatchlings reach deeper water.
Jade and Olive swim to the surface to breathe.
Whoosh! They blow out all the air from their lungs.
Then they suck in a big breath.
Below, everyone starts swimming again.
"Where are we going?" Olive asks.
"I think we'll know when we arrive," Jade says.
"I hope there's good food," Olive says.
The ocean seems to stretch on forever!
Jade and the others swim constantly.
The sea current helps them along.
Finally Jade sees something—a mat of brown seaweed.
"I think we found the place," Jade says.
Olive grins and gulps down some plankton. "Yep!"
Jade and Olive like living in the seaweed.
There's lots of plankton to eat.
Sometimes Jade eats seaweed with her beak.
One day Olive spots a jellyfish. "Can we eat that?"
"Let's find a smaller one," Jade says.
"But first I should go up and breathe.
I'll be right back."
When Jade returns, Olive is gone!
"Olive?" Jade calls. "Where are you?"
She searches, swimming away from the seaweed mat.
Suddenly a huge face looms before her—a barracuda!
"Ahh!" Jade cries.
Barracudas are fast and fierce hunters!
Olive calls her from the seaweed mat. "Jade!"
At the sound, the barracuda spins around.
Jade darts to Olive—and safety. "That was scary!"
Olive nods. "Forget the jellyfish.
Let's stay here and eat more plankton!"
Years later Jade and Olive are living at a reef.
"Time for breakfast!" Jade says.
She crawls out from her sleeping spot under a rock.
The sisters surface to breathe.
When they are active, they must get air often.
But when they are sleeping, it is different.
They can stay underwater for several hours.
Back underwater Jade groans.
"These barnacles are slowing me down!"
Jade's shell is getting harder as she grows.
It's a handy place for barnacles and algae to settle.
"Oh well," Olive says. "Nothing we can do."
A yellow tang fish swims over. "I'm Sunny.
I can clean your shells if you want."
"Really? That would be great," Jade says.
Sunny eats everything on the turtles' shells.
He even cleans algae off their flippers.
Tang fish are important to green sea turtles.
They help them stay healthy.
"Thanks, Sunny," Jade says. "Now let's find breakfast."
Sunny helps the sisters find some algae.
Jade is still hungry.
She finds a patch of seagrass.
Jade's lower jaw is sharp like a saw.
She uses it to tear the seagrass.
When she finishes eating, she tries to leave.
But her flipper is stuck!
"You're caught in a fishing net," Sunny cries.
He looks worried.
Fishing nets can harm sea turtles.
Jade feels it tighten around her flipper. "Help!"
"Stay calm," Olive says.
"But I have to breathe soon!" Jade says.
"Don't panic," Sunny says.
But Jade panics.
She pulls backward and some coral breaks off.
So does the net.
Jade yanks her flipper free.
"Phew!" Jade says.
"Where did that net come from?" Olive asks.
"I don't know," Sunny says.
"But we should stay away from it!"
"Good idea." Jade shudders.
"That net is dangerous.
It doesn't belong on our nice reef.
I hope we don't find one here ever again."
Many years pass.
One day Jade gets a strong feeling.
"We should go."
"Go?" Olive frowns. "Go where?"
"I'm not sure," Jade says. "Somewhere else."
A jellyfish floats past.
Olive gulps it down. "But I like it here."
"This reef is nice," Jade says.
"But we're supposed to be somewhere else now.
I think we'll know the place when we see it."
"Okay." Olive sighs. "Let's go."
The sisters swim away from the reef.
They are much bigger now.
So the open water isn't quite as scary—at first.
"What's that?" Olive cries.
A tiger shark glides past.
Its mouth is full of sharp teeth!
Luckily it is chasing a fish.
Jade and Olive paddle away from the shark.
But they must still be very careful.
The open sea is much more dangerous than the reef.
There's nowhere to hide.
A huge shape—a humpback whale—dives past.
"Wow! I thought we were getting big," Jade says.
The humpback doesn't bother the turtles.
Neither does a manta ray or some dolphins.
"Hi!" A big turtle floats closer. "I'm Lute."
His shell is softer, and his flippers are larger.
Olive's eyes get wide. "Will we grow big like you?"
"Nope," Lute says. "I'm a leatherback sea turtle.
We are bigger and heavier than green sea turtles."
Soon the sisters start swimming again.
At last they reach shallow, calm waters.
Jade spies a sandy beach. "Hey, I know this place.
It's where we hatched!"
Olive nods. "You were right.
This is where we belong."
Soon the two sisters will go back on the beach.
They will make their own nests and lay eggs.
But right now Jade is hungry.
She swims to a field of seagrass. "Let's eat!"
The sun is setting in the Australian Outback.
The red kangaroo mob is on the move.
Bean peeks out of his mother's pouch.
"Where are we going, Mom?" Bean asks.
"We ate all the plants here," Mom says.
"We have to find more food."
"I have plenty of food," Bean says.
He takes a big drink of Mom's milk. "Yum!"
Bean's older brother Rufus hears him.
"Babies like you only drink milk," Rufus says.
"But big kangaroos like me eat grass and other plants!"
Bean frowns. "You're just a little older than me.
But you still drink Mom's milk too.
And I'm not a baby—I'm four months old!"
Rufus laughs. "You are a baby.
You've never been out of Mom's pouch!"
Rufus hops ahead.
"I could eat plants if I wanted to," Bean says.
"Soon, little one," Mom says.
The mob keeps hopping across the Outback.
Suddenly Boomer, the leader, calls out.
"Fresh grass up ahead!"
Rufus starts hopping fast.
But Mom is hungry too.
She uses her powerful back legs to spring forward.
In two big hops, she passes Rufus.
"We win!" Bean says. "Who's the baby now, Rufus?"
"It's still you," Rufus says.
"At least I can hop on my own."
The mob starts grazing.
Mom bends down to eat.
She uses her sharp teeth to bite off grass.
Bean peeks. "The grass looks so close."
He stretches closer and . . .
Bean grabs some grass with his mouth!
Rufus hops over. "Can I have some milk, Mom?"
"Of course," Mom says.
Rufus sticks his head into her pouch for a drink.
"I just ate grass," Bean says proudly.
"Good for you," Rufus says.
Bean grins. "It was yummy.
Soon I'll try other plants!"
Bean watches Rufus playing with a friend.
The joeys are play boxing.
They push with their short front legs.
They kick with their long, strong back legs.
"Time for a race," Rufus says.
"Let's race too, Mom," Bean says.
Mom chuckles and jumps along slowly.
"Faster!" Bean says. "Hurry!"
Mom catches up . . . and leaves the joeys behind!
Bean cheers. "I love being in your pouch.
It's warm and I have lots of milk.
Plus we win every race!"
"Yes," Mom says. "But you're getting big.
Soon you'll have to leave the pouch, like Rufus did."
"We'll see," Bean says.
A few days later, Boomer stomps to warn the mob.
"A wedge-tailed eagle!" he cries. "Protect the joeys!"
Bean ducks lower into Mom's pouch while Rufus stands still.
A huge eagle circles above before flying away.
"Phew, that was scary!" Bean says.
"Good thing I can stay in your pouch, Mom." "That
reminds me," Mom says. "It's
time for you to learn to hop." "No,
thanks." Bean stretches for a bite of grass. But
Mom suddenly tilts forward, and her pouch gets loose. Bean
slides out and lands on the ground. Plop! "Hey!
No fair!" he cries. Mom
hops away. "Wait,
Mom!" Bean cries. "Come back!" He
looks up. What
if the scary eagle returns? Bean's
legs feel wobbly, but he takes a small hop. Another
joey comes over. "Hi, I'm Cookie. Want
to hop together?" "Um
. . ." Bean still feels unsure. "I'll try it." Bean
pushes off with his back legs. His
long tail helps him keep his balance. He
jumps farther this time. "I did it!" Then—
boom!
"Eek!" Bean hops fast to Mom. "I heard thunder!"
He dives headfirst into her pouch.
"Being out was fun," Bean thinks.
"But I like it much better in here!"
The Outback is very hot and dry.
The red kangaroos get some water by eating plants.
Even so, they're getting thirsty.
"Time to go to the watering hole," Mom says.
Bean nods. "I'm ready!"
He finds Cookie and they hop together.
Rufus is ahead of them.
He is hopping fast with his friends.
Mom looks worried. "Stay close, joeys.
There might be dingoes around here."
Soon the mob crosses an open area with no trees.
Cookie looks at Bean. "Are you afraid of dingoes?"
"Yes!" Bean nods. "Mom says they're dangerous wild dogs."
Cookie nods. "They hunt kangaroos!"
Suddenly heat lightning flashes.
It lights up a dark shape.
"A dingo!" Bean cries.
Boomer thumps his feet to warn the mob.
Then he stands up very straight.
"Boomer is making himself look really big!" Bean thinks.
Boomer growls at the dingo. "Stay away from our mob!"
Bean hops over to Mom and paws at her pouch.
"Let me in!"
Finally she bends down.
The mob starts moving again.
Suddenly howling rises in the distance. Whoo!
Bean peeks out—there's a whole pack of dingoes now!
The first dingo runs to join the pack.
They all disappear into the darkness.
"Will they come back?" Bean asks nervously.
"I don't think so," Mom says.
"You can come out again."
"Maybe I'll just stay in here," Bean says.
"No, Bean," Mom says.
"We haven't reached the watering hole yet.
And you're getting too heavy to carry."
"Okay." Bean sighs and crawls out.
With her claws, Mom gently grooms him.
She is keeping his fur clean.
"You're big and brave now," she whispers.
Bean smiles and hops off to find Cookie.
"Those dingoes were scary," she says.
"Yeah," Bean says.
"But not too scary for brave kangaroos like us!"
"Are we there yet?" Bean asks.
"We'll reach the watering hole tomorrow," Mom says.
"I'm so hot!" Bean moans.
Mom tells him to lick his arms to stay cool.
Bean lies down to sleep.
He licks his arms again, then drifts off.
Later Bean wakes to stomping and loud cries.
Stomp! Stomp! Boomer is sending out a warning.
"Fire!" someone else cries.
"Mom?" Bean leaps to his feet. "Where are you?"
His heart thumps with fear.
He wants to get in Mom's pouch!
"Hurry!" Cookie hops past. "We have to escape the fire!"
"Wait!" Bean hops as fast as he can.
The fire follows the mob, gobbling up the dry plants.
Finally Bean spots her. "Mom! Let me in!"
Mom shakes her head. "No more pouch, Bean.
You're too big—you must hop on your own."
With a groan, Bean starts hopping again.
Soon he catches up to Rufus.
"Good job, little brother," Rufus says.
"We need to move fast."
At last the mob leaves the fire behind.
"Bean, are you okay?" Cookie asks.
Bean nods.
"I was scared at first, but I'm a fast jumper!"
Mom nods proudly.
"You don't need to ride in my pouch anymore."
"The watering hole is just ahead!" Boomer calls.
Everyone hops forward.
Other mobs are already there.
But there's plenty of water and food for everyone.
A few weeks later, Bean and Rufus are racing.
Bean laughs. "I'm thirsty!"
He finds Mom and asks for some milk.
"Sure," she says. "But be careful.
There's a surprise in my pouch."
"Huh?" Bean sticks his head inside.
A tiny, hairless baby is sleeping there!
"That's your sister Tilly," Mom says.
"Hi, Tilly," Bean says. "You're small now.
But someday you'll be big and fast—just like me!"
It's morning in the cold ocean.
Koda, a sea otter pup, floats on her mother's belly.
Nearby, other pups float with their moms too.
Koda drinks Mom's milk.
She feels full and happy.
"Time for grooming!" Mom says.
Mom blows air bubbles into Koda's fluffy baby fur.
The air bubbles trap warm air.
This keeps Koda warm and dry in the cold water.
"I'm going hunting now," Mom says.
"But . . ." Koda gulps. "I don't want you to leave."
Mom smiles. "You know I'll be back soon!"
The sea otters live near an underwater kelp forest.
Mom wraps Koda tightly in some kelp.
"That's so you won't float away!"
Mom dives underwater.
Koda hears a pup crying for his mom.
"I'm okay," Koda thinks. "Floating is fun."
The air trapped in Koda's soft fur helps her float.
Her webbed feet feel warm in the sun. Suddenly
a shadow passes overhead! "A
bald eagle!" Koda thinks. The
eagle has a sharp beak and huge wings. It
swoops down! "Weee!"
Koda cries for Mom. She
tries to move, but the kelp holds her tightly! "Weee!"
Koda cries again. Suddenly—
splash! Mom pops up.
She unwraps Koda and wraps her leg around the pup.
Together they swim away fast.
"I was so scared!" Koda says.
"I'm glad I heard your cry," Mom says.
"Look—I found a clam."
Mom floats on her back, holding the clam.
Then she reaches under one arm.
Like other sea otters, Mom has a special pocket there.
She pulls out a rock.
She lays it on her belly.
Mom bangs the clam against the rock. Smash!
It cracks open.
Mom eats some clam meat and gives some to Koda.
Koda grins. "Mmm!"
"Koda," Mom says. "You can swim and dive now.
It's time to hunt on your own."
"No way!" Koda says. "I can't hunt!"
Mom laughs. "I'll teach you."
They dive underwater.
Koda's baby fur is gone.
Now she has a sleek, dark coat.
Its thick layers keep her warm in the cold water.
Koda waves to Niko, another pup.
He's learning to hunt too.
Koda's nostrils and ears close to keep water out.
She can see the ocean floor very clearly.
"Cool!" she thinks.
Koda watches Mom grab a sea urchin with her claws.
Mom tucks it into her pocket.
Then they swim back to the surface.
"Time to eat." Mom pulls a rock from her pocket.
"Do I need a rock?" Koda asks.
Mom nods. "Hunters need tools to crack shells."
First, Mom rubs off the urchin's spines.
Next, she bangs the urchin on her rock.
Mom and Koda eat the tasty snack.
"It's your turn to hunt now," Mom says.
They dive underwater.
Koda bends her body and tail to swim fast.
Suddenly a school of fish stirs up silt.
The water turns dark.
"I can't see!" Koda says.
"Use your whiskers and paws," Mom says.
Koda feels her whiskers twitch—something is swimming by!
Koda reaches out but catches nothing.
Koda swims up for air and sighs. "Hunting is hard!"
"Keep trying," Mom says.
Koda dives to the ocean floor again.
With her paws, she feels a smooth rock.
"A tool!" Koda puts the rock in her pocket.
Suddenly a crab crawls across the floor below her.
Koda grabs it and swims up.
"Use your rock," Mom says.
Koda bangs the crab against the rock. Crack!
Koda shares the crabmeat with Mom.
"Koda!" Niko calls. "I can hunt now!"
Koda grins. "Me too!"
Koda floats with a group of moms and pups.
The otters hold paws so they don't float away.
These "rafts" keep them safe and warm.
But Koda gets bored just floating around.
"Niko, let's play!" Koda says.
The two pups swim away from the raft.
They twist and dive and chase each other.
Suddenly someone grabs Koda by the scruff of her neck.
"Koda!" Mom pulls Koda back to the raft.
"You must stay close," Mom says.
"Sharks hunt for sea otter pups."
Mom starts grooming Koda.
"Mom treats me like a baby," Koda thinks.
She pulls away from Mom. "I can do it myself!"
Otters have thicker fur than any other animal.
So they must groom it often.
First, Koda licks her fur.
Next, she combs it with her claws.
She twists in circles to reach every spot.
"There!" she thinks. "Warm and dry!"
Niko's mom, Luti, is about to go hunting.
"Come on, Koda!" Niko calls.
Koda dives underwater too.
Luti pries a mollusk off a ledge with her rock.
Niko pulls a snail off some kelp.
Koda digs up a clam.
They swim back to the raft.
"Good job hunting, Koda," Mom says.
"Thanks," Koda says.
"Luti and Niko eat different foods than we do."
"Right." Mom nods. "That way there's enough food for everyone."
"Oh," Koda says.
Koda bangs the clam against her rock.
Seagulls fly overhead.
"Watch out for the gulls," Mom says.
Koda doesn't listen.
She cracks open the shell and pulls out meat.
Suddenly a gull swoops down.
It grabs Koda's clam and flies away!
"Here." Mom gives Koda some food.
"Thanks!" Koda says.
She reaches for Mom's paw.
"I still need Mom," Koda thinks. "And the raft."
One day Mom smiles at Koda. "You're getting bigger.
My big job of raising you is almost done."
Koda nods as they float together.
"I want a big job," she thinks.
Soon Niko swims by. "Hey, Koda, let's go hunting."
"Good idea," Koda says.
They swim underwater through the kelp forest.
They see fish, squid, octopuses, and sea urchins.
"There's so much food here!" Koda thinks.
They eat some fish.
"Now let's explore," Niko says.
The pups swim away from the kelp forest.
They've never been this far from home.
They dive underwater.
"Wow!" Koda thinks.
She sees a carpet of sea urchins.
"But where's all the kelp?" she thinks.
"And no other sea creatures are here!"
Koda and Niko come up for air.
"Nobody lives here," Koda says.
Niko nods. "I don't like this place."
"Me neither," Koda says. "Let's go!"
Later Koda tells Mom about the strange place.
"There was no kelp—and no other animals."
Mom nods. "You saw an urchin barren."
"A . . . what?" Koda asks.
"It's a place that sea urchins take over," Mom says.
"They eat all the kelp."
"But . . ." Koda frowns. "Otters need kelp forests.
So do other animals."
Mom nods. "Sea otters eat lots of sea urchins.
That keeps the kelp forest strong and healthy."
Later Koda and Niko dive underwater.
They catch starfish, squid, and sea urchins.
They float on their backs and eat.
Suddenly Koda realizes something.
Koda tells Niko about the urchin barren.
"So our job is to eat sea urchins!" Niko says.
"Yep!" Koda pulls out her rock. "It's a big job.
Let's get to work!"
